minutes.headline: Charter committee proposed a two-day Town Meeting (May 4 and 6) and settled how to present charter changes at the Feb 27 hearing.
minutes.summary: The Charter Review Committee announced a tentative plan to hold Town Meeting over two days, with all charter articles taken up on May 6, and members questioned the plan. Members spent most of the meeting on the color-coding of proposed changes (typographical, substantive, town clerk and select board), the format of the Feb 27 public hearing, and specific charter sections. A motion on the planning director appointment timeline was taken, and the town clerk grandfather clause and unemployment questions were discussed.

decisions.decision: Tentative plan announced: Town Meeting on Saturday May 4 for non-charter articles, adjourned to Monday May 6 at 7 p.m. at the high school/middle school auditorium for the four charter articles; feedback to be taken before it is final.
The question of the capital budget language in section 4.2 (struck from the original) will be placed on the Feb 27 agenda with a star for the full committee.
A member agreed to write the pro and con for keeping the town clerk appointed; the chair to receive it by Feb 27.
The chair will prepare an original-format charter with line numbers and a version showing only purple and brown changes for the public hearing, and ask about side-by-side screens.
At the Feb 27 hearing, the committee will go through the charter section by section, hearing public questions as it goes, without deliberating or voting.

what_happened.line: The Charter Review Committee announced a tentative two-day Town Meeting: non-charter articles on a Saturday, then the four charter articles on a Monday evening, pending feedback.
The committee agreed that at the Feb 27 public hearing it will go section by section, take public questions as it goes, and neither deliberate nor vote.
A motion to move the planning director appointment to thirty days after notice, rather than fifteen, was taken; the outcome was not audible.
The cost of making the town clerk an appointed position, including unemployment compensation and benefits, was raised as a question voters will ask and left to be researched.
Section 4.2 capital budget language will go on the Feb 27 agenda for the full committee, and a member will write the pro and con on an appointed clerk.

why_it_matters: Charter changes, including whether the town clerk becomes appointed rather than elected, go to Town Meeting voters, and the cost of that change had not yet been worked out at this meeting.
The Feb 27 hearing is the stage where residents can ask questions on each section, but the committee will not deliberate or vote there.
